attribution: Taxonomy and 5-slot camera prompt structure inspired by Dan Kieft (aicameramovements.com / YouTube 7GWd4PV3hoA). Prompts and dramatic intent guidelines written in original prose for Video Factory.

grammar.template: Camera: <move name & mount>. Movement: <physical trajectory or optical change>. Speed: <pacing & dynamics>. Framing: <subject lock, horizon & parallax rules>. End: <landing composition>.

moves.name: Static shot
moves.intent: Directs undivided attention to the subject or performance inside the frame without camera distraction; creates composure, observational neutrality, or deadpan tension.
moves.when_to_use: Dialogue holds, deadpan comedy beats, dense visual tableaux, or opening/closing frames where motion inside the scene carries the beat.
moves.prompt: Camera: locked tripod static shot. Movement: remain completely stationary from a single fixed vantage point for the entire duration. Speed: zero camera motion, rock-steady hold. Framing: preserve the exact starting lens focal length, camera elevation, horizon line, and spatial composition. End: conclude on the identical locked frame without drift.

moves.name: Pan right
moves.intent: Scans laterally across space or connects a subject to something previously off-screen on the right, guiding viewer curiosity across the horizon.
moves.when_to_use: Room reveals, following a character crossing left-to-right, or linking cause on the left to consequence on the right.
moves.prompt: Camera: tripod-mounted horizontal pan right. Movement: pivot the lens smoothly from left to right around a fixed nodal axis without translating the tripod base. Speed: steady, measured rotational sweep. Framing: maintain a level horizon while off-screen environment enters cleanly from the right edge of the frame. End: come to a gentle, balanced stop on the rightward composition.

moves.name: Pan left
moves.intent: Sweeps attention leftward across an environment or follows right-to-left action to uncover off-screen context.
moves.when_to_use: Scanning wide interiors or landscapes from right to left, tracking an actor's glance toward the left edge, or revealing a hidden witness.
moves.prompt: Camera: tripod-mounted horizontal pan left. Movement: pivot the lens smoothly from right to left around a fixed nodal axis without shifting the camera position. Speed: steady, measured rotational sweep. Framing: maintain a level horizon while new visual space enters cleanly from the left edge of the frame. End: come to a gentle, balanced stop on the leftward composition.

moves.name: Whip pan right
moves.intent: Injects sudden kinetic energy, surprise, or comic timing by snapping attention violently to a second subject on the right.
moves.when_to_use: High-tempo reaction cuts, rapid topic transitions, sudden reveals of an eavesdropper, or punchline juxtaposition.
moves.prompt: Camera: high-speed whip pan right. Movement: snap the lens horizontally from the initial axis toward a secondary target on the right. Speed: rapid rotational burst producing brief directional motion blur mid-sweep. Framing: start on a clear opening subject and lock abruptly onto a distinct second composition on the right. End: arrest the rotation cleanly on a sharp, stable final frame.

moves.name: Whip pan left
moves.intent: Snaps viewer focus abruptly leftward with a streak of motion blur, creating urgency, shock, or rhythmic punch.
moves.when_to_use: Fast conversational ping-pong, sudden alarms off-screen left, or energetic transitional bridges between two moments.
moves.prompt: Camera: high-speed whip pan left. Movement: snap the lens horizontally from the initial axis toward a secondary target on the left. Speed: rapid rotational burst producing brief directional motion blur mid-sweep. Framing: start on a clear opening subject and lock abruptly onto a distinct second composition on the left. End: arrest the rotation cleanly on a sharp, stable final frame.

moves.name: Tilt up
moves.intent: Builds awe, scale, dominance, or aspiration by guiding the eye vertically from ground level toward towering height.
moves.when_to_use: Character introductions from boots to face, revealing monumental architecture or towering trees, or following a subject's upward gaze.
moves.prompt: Camera: fixed-base vertical tilt up. Movement: pivot the lens upward from a stationary mount without raising the physical camera height. Speed: smooth, continuous upward rotation. Framing: keep the vertical axis of the subject or structure aligned near center as upper space enters the top of frame. End: settle cleanly on the elevated target composition.

moves.name: Tilt down
moves.intent: Grounds a scene from height down to intimate detail, or emphasizes vulnerability, defeat, or a hidden clue on the floor.
moves.when_to_use: Transitioning from a skyline or ceiling down to street action, following a dropped object, or revealing footwear/ground details.
moves.prompt: Camera: fixed-base vertical tilt down. Movement: pivot the lens downward from a stationary mount without lowering the physical camera height. Speed: smooth, continuous downward rotation. Framing: keep the vertical subject or architectural line centered as lower ground detail enters the bottom of frame. End: settle cleanly on the lower target composition.

moves.name: Slow zoom in
moves.intent: Gradually ratchets psychological tension and intimacy, drawing the viewer inexorably into a character's internal realization or confession.
moves.when_to_use: Monologues, tense confessions, creeping dread, or isolating a key detail while keeping flat optical perspective.
moves.prompt: Camera: optical slow zoom in from a fixed tripod position. Movement: smoothly lengthen the lens focal length to magnify the central subject without moving the camera body in space. Speed: slow, imperceptibly steady creep. Framing: keep the primary subject anchored and sharp as surrounding context narrows away. End: hold on a stable, tighter framing of the target.

moves.name: Slow zoom out
moves.intent: Creates emotional detachment, solitude, or growing perspective by revealing how small the subject is within their wider surroundings.
moves.when_to_use: End-of-chapter beats, revealing a vast or indifferent setting around a lone figure, or reframing an intimate detail into full context.
moves.prompt: Camera: optical slow zoom out from a fixed tripod position. Movement: smoothly shorten the lens focal length toward a wider field of view without moving the camera body. Speed: slow, even optical pullback. Framing: keep the initial subject readable at center while progressive layers of surrounding environment enter the edges. End: hold on a stable, wider establishing composition.

moves.name: Fast zoom in
moves.intent: Punctuates a sudden discovery, reality check, or sharp shift in attention without the full cartoon aggression of a crash zoom.
moves.when_to_use: Moment of recognition, spotting an error or hazard across a room, or emphasizing a sudden vulnerability in a speaker's face.
moves.prompt: Camera: optical fast zoom in. Movement: rapidly increase lens focal length from a stationary camera position toward the focal subject. Speed: brisk, decisive optical push. Framing: maintain crisp center alignment on the target as the field of view tightens quickly. End: lock onto a firm, close composition without rebound.

moves.name: Fast zoom out
moves.intent: Rapidly recontextualizes a close detail into a surprising wider reality, delivering an immediate sense of exposure or shift in scale.
moves.when_to_use: Sudden situational reveals, breaking out of a tight focus into a busy room, or quick rhythmic widening on a musical accent.
moves.prompt: Camera: optical fast zoom out. Movement: rapidly decrease lens focal length from a stationary camera position away from the focal subject. Speed: brisk, decisive optical widen. Framing: keep the starting subject legible as the surrounding room or landscape expands into frame. End: lock onto a stable, wide composition.

moves.name: Crash zoom in
moves.intent: Delivers maximum visceral shock, melodramatic intensity, or comedic punch by slamming the viewer straight into the subject's eyes or detail.
moves.when_to_use: Tarantino/action shock beats, sudden overwhelming realizations, comedic double-takes, or hard musical drops.
moves.prompt: Camera: aggressive crash zoom in. Movement: snap the lens focal length violently from wide to tight on the primary target without translating the camera. Speed: explosive, instantaneous optical slam. Framing: keep the target dead-center and readable through the rapid focal compression. End: stick hard on a bold, tight close-up.

moves.name: Crash zoom out
moves.intent: Unveils an absurd, chaotic, or shocking wider situation in an instant, often for comedic contrast or sudden spatial disorientation.
moves.when_to_use: Visual punchlines where a serious close-up sits inside a ridiculous setting, or abrupt reveals of surrounding danger.
moves.prompt: Camera: aggressive crash zoom out. Movement: snap the lens focal length violently from a tight close-up to a wide view from a fixed position. Speed: explosive, instantaneous optical pullback. Framing: preserve the central subject's readability as the chaotic or expansive environment bursts into frame around them. End: stick hard on a bold, wide composition.

moves.name: Dolly in
moves.intent: Physically steps the audience closer into the scene with real 3D parallax, creating earned intimacy, gravitas, or mounting suspense.
moves.when_to_use: Approaching a character at a turning point, creeping down a corridor toward a mystery, or landing a pivotal statement.
moves.prompt: Camera: physical dolly in on a linear track. Movement: translate the entire camera body smoothly forward through three-dimensional space toward the subject at fixed focal length. Speed: measured, deliberate forward glide. Framing: maintain constant lens height and aim while foreground elements separate with natural parallax as distance closes. End: settle cleanly into a closer, intimate framing.

moves.name: Dolly out
moves.intent: Physically retreats from the subject with true spatial parallax, evoking abandonment, loneliness, defeat, or quiet reflection.
moves.when_to_use: Leaving a character isolated in their environment, closing a poignant scene, or revealing foreground space as the camera backs away.
moves.prompt: Camera: physical dolly out on a linear track. Movement: translate the entire camera body smoothly backward through three-dimensional space away from the subject at fixed focal length. Speed: measured, controlled backward retreat. Framing: keep camera elevation and optical axis constant while foreground and surrounding environment expand into view with natural parallax. End: settle cleanly into a wider, distanced composition.

moves.name: Truck right
moves.intent: Generates rich three-dimensional depth by sliding laterally past foreground and background planes, showcasing layout or parallel progression.
moves.when_to_use: Moving alongside a wall, lineup, or table, pacing a character walking left-to-right, or gliding across an architectural facade.
moves.prompt: Camera: lateral truck right on a straight track. Movement: translate the entire camera body horizontally to the right while keeping the lens pointed perpendicular to the direction of travel. Speed: smooth, constant sideways glide. Framing: preserve level horizon and fixed forward aim as foreground, midground, and background planes slide past at different parallax speeds. End: finish on a balanced lateral composition.

moves.name: Truck left
moves.intent: Slides laterally leftward through space with full parallax separation, revealing adjacent rooms, workstations, or parallel action.
moves.when_to_use: Exploring a cross-section of a set from right to left, pacing right-to-left motion, or unveiling a scene behind a vertical divider.
moves.prompt: Camera: lateral truck left on a straight track. Movement: translate the entire camera body horizontally to the left while keeping the lens pointed perpendicular to the direction of travel. Speed: smooth, constant sideways glide. Framing: preserve level horizon and fixed forward aim as foreground, midground, and background planes slide past at different parallax speeds. End: finish on a balanced lateral composition.

moves.name: Pedestal up
moves.intent: Rises straight up on a vertical column without tilting the lens, revealing a subject's full stature or emerging above a foreground barrier.
moves.when_to_use: Vertical character introductions from ground to eye level, rising above a desk or wall to see what lies beyond, or dignified elevation.
moves.prompt: Camera: vertical pedestal up. Movement: elevate the entire camera body straight upward along a vertical axis without tilting the lens up or down. Speed: smooth, uniform vertical rise. Framing: keep the optical axis level and parallel to the ground while the view climbs from lower details to the upper composition. End: hold cleanly at the elevated camera height.

moves.name: Pedestal down
moves.intent: Descends straight down on a vertical column with a level lens, sinking below eye level or dropping behind a foreground surface.
moves.when_to_use: Lowering from eye level to desk/floor height, descending below a table edge to reveal hidden action, or grounding a transition.
moves.prompt: Camera: vertical pedestal down. Movement: lower the entire camera body straight downward along a vertical axis without tilting the lens up or down. Speed: smooth, uniform vertical descent. Framing: keep the optical axis level and parallel to the ground while the view drops toward the lower plane. End: hold cleanly at the lowered camera height.

moves.name: Slider right
moves.intent: Adds subtle, high-craft cinematic parallax across a short lateral span, making intimate or tabletop scenes feel tactile and three-dimensional.
moves.when_to_use: Close/medium shots of a person working at a desk, product/prop detail shots, or quiet dialogue where a full truck shot would overwhelm.
moves.prompt: Camera: short-rail slider right. Movement: glide the camera a compact distance to the right along a precision slider rail. Speed: slow, silky, micro-controlled lateral motion. Framing: let near foreground objects shift gently against the subject and background to create refined three-dimensional parallax. End: settle on a composed slight right-angle perspective.

moves.name: Slider left
moves.intent: Introduces delicate leftward parallax in tight spaces, keeping a quiet or detailed shot visually alive without drawing attention to the rig.
moves.when_to_use: Intimate portraits, evidence or craft table inspection, or subtle reframing during a thoughtful pause.
moves.prompt: Camera: short-rail slider left. Movement: glide the camera a compact distance to the left along a precision slider rail. Speed: slow, silky, micro-controlled lateral motion. Framing: let near foreground objects shift gently against the subject and background to create refined three-dimensional parallax. End: settle on a composed slight left-angle perspective.

moves.name: Push past / pass-by shot
moves.intent: Creates voyeuristic discovery and deep spatial immersion by moving past an obstructing foreground element into a hidden or active room.
moves.when_to_use: Entering a doorway, gliding past hanging cables/pillars/foliage to discover a character at work, or revealing a secret moment.
moves.prompt: Camera: forward push-past shot. Movement: advance the camera physically forward past a prominent foreground object, doorframe, or obstacle into the open space beyond. Speed: smooth, continuous forward glide. Framing: allow the foreground element to sweep closely past the edge of the lens as the main subject in the deeper plane comes into unobstructed view. End: arrive cleanly inside the revealed space beyond the foreground layer.

moves.name: Arc right
moves.intent: Wraps partially around the subject toward the right, shifting the viewer's perspective from behind or profile to a revealing front/three-quarter angle.
moves.when_to_use: Pivotal dialogue turns, shifting from a character's back to their facial reaction, or showcasing a subject from a changing dramatic angle.
moves.prompt: Camera: curved arc right around subject. Movement: travel along a shallow circular track to the right while keeping the lens aimed inward at the primary subject. Speed: smooth, measured curved glide. Framing: maintain consistent subject distance, camera elevation, and center framing while the background sweeps leftward behind them. End: settle on the new right-side perspective.

moves.name: Arc left
moves.intent: Wraps partially around the subject toward the left, dynamically re-angling the scene and rotating the background for dimensional emphasis.
moves.when_to_use: Revealing what a character is looking at by arcing around their shoulder, or energizing a static conversation.
moves.prompt: Camera: curved arc left around subject. Movement: travel along a shallow circular track to the left while keeping the lens aimed inward at the primary subject. Speed: smooth, measured curved glide. Framing: maintain consistent subject distance, camera elevation, and center framing while the background sweeps rightward behind them. End: settle on the new left-side perspective.

moves.name: Orbit clockwise
moves.intent: Encircles the subject completely like a planetary center of gravity, heightening heroism, disorientation, romance, or surreal spectacle.
moves.when_to_use: Heroic standoffs, climactic realizations, magical/fantasy reveals, or high-intensity emotional peaks.
moves.prompt: Camera: 360-degree clockwise orbit. Movement: revolve continuously clockwise around the central subject at a fixed radius while keeping the lens locked inward on them. Speed: fluid, sustained orbital motion. Framing: hold the subject anchored in the center of the frame as the entire surrounding environment rotates smoothly around them. End: complete the orbital arc on a balanced, stable composition.

moves.name: Orbit counterclockwise
moves.intent: Surrounds the subject in a sweeping counterclockwise rotation, isolating them at the eye of a dynamic, swirling world.
moves.when_to_use: Action showcases, euphoric musical bridges, or reversing orbital momentum between cuts.
moves.prompt: Camera: 360-degree counterclockwise orbit. Movement: revolve continuously counterclockwise around the central subject at a fixed radius while keeping the lens locked inward on them. Speed: fluid, sustained orbital motion. Framing: hold the subject anchored in the center of the frame as the entire surrounding environment rotates smoothly around them. End: complete the orbital arc on a balanced, stable composition.

moves.name: Tracking shot
moves.intent: Travels through the environment in lockstep with a moving subject, placing the audience inside the momentum of their journey.
moves.when_to_use: Characters striding through busy workspaces, corridors, or streets where subject and surroundings share narrative weight.
moves.prompt: Camera: stabilized tracking shot. Movement: travel physically through the environment along the same path and vector as the moving subject. Speed: synchronized precisely to the subject's travel pace. Framing: keep the subject at a constant size and position in frame while the surrounding setting flows past. End: sustain the balanced moving composition through the end of the beat.

moves.name: Follow shot / over-the-shoulder
moves.intent: Aligns the audience directly behind the character so we experience the unfolding corridor, mystery, or destination exactly as they approach it.
moves.when_to_use: Entering unknown spaces, walking down dark stairs or hallways, or building anticipation before a reveal.
moves.prompt: Camera: rear follow shot at shoulder elevation. Movement: advance directly behind the subject along their forward path. Speed: matched evenly to the subject's walking stride. Framing: anchor the subject's back, shoulders, and head in the foreground/midground while keeping the route and destination ahead clearly visible. End: continue trailing smoothly with the subject leading the frame.

moves.name: Reverse tracking / walk-and-talk
moves.intent: Locks onto the subject's face and emotional expression while they advance forward, combining forward narrative drive with intimate facial access.
moves.when_to_use: Walk-and-talk dialogue, determined marches toward camera, or singing/speaking directly while moving through a location.
moves.prompt: Camera: reverse tracking lead shot. Movement: retreat smoothly backward along the path directly in front of a forward-walking subject. Speed: synchronized to the subject's forward pace to preserve constant camera-to-subject distance. Framing: keep the subject's face and upper body sharp and centered while the background recedes behind them. End: hold the steady front-facing moving composition.

moves.name: Side tracking
moves.intent: Showcases athletic stride, speed, and profile determination against a streaking lateral backdrop.
moves.when_to_use: Runners, walkers in profile, side-view travel sequences, or emphasizing directional velocity across a landscape.
moves.prompt: Camera: parallel side-tracking shot. Movement: travel laterally alongside the moving subject on a parallel path. Speed: matched exactly to the subject's horizontal speed. Framing: hold the subject in clean side or three-quarter profile at a constant distance while the background streaks horizontally past. End: maintain the locked parallel composition in motion.

moves.name: Low tracking
moves.intent: Builds mystery, swagger, or kinetic immediacy by withholding the character's face and focusing on boots, wheels, paws, or ground-level action.
moves.when_to_use: Mysterious character arrivals, rhythmic footstep shots on beat, skateboard/wheel close-ups, or tense ground-level pursuits.
moves.prompt: Camera: low-altitude ground tracking shot. Movement: glide close to the ground plane below waist height along the subject's travel vector. Speed: synchronized to the cadence of footsteps, wheels, or low-level motion. Framing: keep boots, wheels, or lower-body mechanics sharp in frame while the textured ground surface rushes beneath the lens. End: preserve the low-angle moving perspective cleanly.

moves.name: Vehicle tracking
moves.intent: Captures high-velocity automotive, cycle, or train travel while keeping the machine razor-sharp against a rushing road and landscape.
moves.when_to_use: Highway travel sequences, chase setups, motorcycle rides, or arrival/departure transitions.
moves.prompt: Camera: stabilized vehicle-to-vehicle tracking shot. Movement: travel at speed alongside or ahead of the moving vehicle along its roadway path. Speed: matched precisely to the vehicle's velocity. Framing: hold the vehicle crisp and anchored in frame while the road surface and environment blur past with genuine speed. End: maintain a clean, high-speed rolling composition.

moves.name: Chase shot
moves.intent: Drops the audience into breathless pursuit with urgent, reactive momentum that scrambles to keep up with unpredictable action.
moves.when_to_use: Escape sequences, action sprints, frantic pursuits through obstacles, or high-adrenaline climax beats.
moves.prompt: Camera: kinetic close-pursuit chase shot. Movement: rush rapidly behind or alongside a fleeing subject along an erratic action path. Speed: fast, urgent, and physically reactive to sudden turns. Framing: keep the moving subject visible in frame while allowing energetic, breathless reframing and close obstacle pass-bys. End: stay tightly locked onto the subject's momentum.

moves.name: Handheld shot
moves.intent: Strips away robotic AI polish in favor of raw human presence, documentary immediacy, or interpersonal tension.
moves.when_to_use: Heated arguments, intimate verite moments, nervous energy, or any scene where mechanical perfection feels sterile.
moves.prompt: Camera: human-operated shoulder/handheld camera. Movement: hold the camera at natural operator eye level with subtle, organic breathing and weight shifts. Speed: responsive, living micro-movements rather than mechanical glide. Framing: keep the subject clearly framed while allowing gentle, authentic human sway and reactive micro-corrections. End: finish on a natural, lived-in handheld composition.

moves.name: Body-mounted camera / Snorricam
moves.intent: Induces visceral panic, intoxication, vertigo, or psychological overload by freezing the actor's face dead-center while the world convulses around them.
moves.when_to_use: Panic attacks, disorientation, chaotic crowd stumbles, psychological breakdowns, or frantic music-video performance hooks.
moves.prompt: Camera: body-mounted Snorricam harnessed to the subject's chest pointing back at their face. Movement: travel locked rigidly to the subject's torso as they stumble, turn, or move through space. Speed: coupled 1:1 to every jolt and rotation of the subject's body. Framing: keep the subject's face and upper torso locked in the exact center of frame while the background tilts, spins, and lurches around them. End: conclude with the subject still frozen at center against the shifting room.

moves.name: Crane up
moves.intent: Lifts the audience skyward out of an intimate human moment into sweeping geographic scale, delivering liberation, grandeur, or poignant finality.
moves.when_to_use: Scene/film endings, transitioning from a lone character to a vast cityscape or horizon, or orchestral swells.
moves.prompt: Camera: sweeping mechanical crane up. Movement: rise smoothly from ground level high into open space along a grand vertical arc. Speed: slow, majestic upward lift. Framing: keep the starting subject or landmark visible as the camera climbs above roofs or obstacles to unveil the wider world. End: settle on a commanding high-angle vista.

moves.name: Crane down
moves.intent: Descends from grand establishing scale right down to a single human protagonist or detail, Funneling wide context into personal story.
moves.when_to_use: Opening a scene or chapter by dropping from a skyline/crowd down to the main character at street level.
moves.prompt: Camera: sweeping mechanical crane down. Movement: descend smoothly from an elevated vantage point down through open space toward ground level. Speed: slow, controlled vertical drop. Framing: transition cleanly from the wide establishing overview down onto the specific subject or mark below. End: settle into a stable eye-level or medium composition on the target.

moves.name: Drone push in
moves.intent: Flies effortlessly across altitude and terrain toward a landmark or subject, bridging epic geography with a specific destination.
moves.when_to_use: Approaching a building, island, vehicle, or rooftop subject from the air; threading into a location.
moves.prompt: Camera: stabilized aerial drone push in. Movement: fly smoothly forward through open airspace on a descending or level glide toward the destination target. Speed: fluid, continuous aerial approach. Framing: keep the landmark or subject centered as surrounding terrain sweeps beneath and past the lens. End: arrive at a closer, composed aerial framing of the target.

moves.name: Drone pull back
moves.intent: Retreats into the sky away from the subject to unveil the breathtaking scale of the landscape, ocean, or city surrounding them.
moves.when_to_use: Epic scale reveals, cliffside/rooftop/desert isolation shots, or closing aerial outros.
moves.prompt: Camera: stabilized aerial drone pull back. Movement: fly smoothly backward and slightly upward away from the subject through open airspace. Speed: controlled, expansive aerial retreat. Framing: keep the starting subject readable near center as vast surrounding landscape or architecture opens up around them. End: finish on a sweeping wide aerial vista.

moves.name: Helicopter shot
moves.intent: Commands theatrical, big-budget scale with a heavy, ultra-steady high-altitude cruise over coastlines, mountain ranges, or sprawling skylines.
moves.when_to_use: Grand opening titles, establishing a massive world or highway journey from high altitude.
moves.prompt: Camera: gyro-stabilized high-altitude helicopter aerial. Movement: cruise along a broad, sweeping flight path high above the terrain or skyline. Speed: steady, unhurried, monumental aerial momentum. Framing: hold the expansive landscape or distant moving vehicle in crisp wide-scale proportion with a rock-solid horizon. End: sustain the grand high-altitude establishing frame.

moves.name: First-person view
moves.intent: Puts the audience directly inside the protagonist's skull so every step, reach, and threshold crossing is felt firsthand.
moves.when_to_use: Subjective exploration, interacting with objects by hand, entering a room through a character's eyes, or immersive transitions.
moves.prompt: Camera: subjective first-person POV at human eye height. Movement: advance forward with the natural cadence of a person walking or reaching into the scene. Speed: authentic human stride and head turn pace. Framing: include subtle peripheral cues like the character's reaching hands or forearms entering frame as they interact with the space ahead. End: arrive directly at the point of interaction from the character's eye line.

moves.name: Tilt-shift
moves.intent: Transforms a full-scale real-world city, harbor, or crowd into a charming, toy-like miniature diorama through selective plane focus.
moves.when_to_use: Stylized city overviews, playful establishing shots, or making complex industrial/urban systems look like a tabletop model.
moves.prompt: Camera: high-angle tilt-shift miniature lens shot. Movement: hold steady or drift slightly from an elevated isometric vantage looking down at the scene. Speed: calm, subtle observation. Framing: render a razor-thin horizontal band of crisp focus across the center subject while throwing the upper background and lower foreground into creamy optical blur for a toy-model scale illusion. End: hold the diorama-like miniature composition intact.

moves.name: Infinite zoom
moves.intent: Creates a hypnotic, dreamlike tunnel effect where zooming through the center of one world continuously unveils another nested world inside it.
moves.when_to_use: Surreal transitions, mind-bending conceptual hooks, dream sequences, or visual metaphors of hidden layers.
moves.prompt: Camera: continuous center-locked infinite zoom. Movement: drive endlessly forward through the exact geometric center of the frame as nested portals or frames expand past the edges. Speed: smooth, hypnotic, continuously accelerating inward push. Framing: keep the central aperture aligned dead-center as each outer environment gives way to the inner world. End: conclude when the newly revealed inner scene fills the entire frame.

moves.name: Earth zoom out
moves.intent: Compressed cosmic perspective shift—rocketing vertically from a single person or rooftop through neighborhood, city, continent, and out to planetary orbit.
moves.when_to_use: Global scale statements, connecting one local human story to worldwide impact, or dramatic finale pullbacks.
moves.prompt: Camera: vertical macro-to-planetary earth zoom out. Movement: rocket straight upward from the ground subject through roof level, city grid, cloud layer, and into orbital altitude. Speed: rapid, exponentially accelerating vertical pullback. Framing: keep the origin point centered directly beneath the lens as concentric rings of geography expand outward. End: finish on a high-altitude or planetary view with the starting location anchored at center.

moves.name: Time-lapse
moves.intent: Compresses hours of changing light, weather, traffic, or construction into seconds while the camera remains monumentally still.
moves.when_to_use: Showing passage of time, day-to-night transitions, bustling crowd/traffic energy, or environmental transformation.
moves.prompt: Camera: locked-off tripod time-lapse. Movement: keep the camera body and lens completely motionless from a single fixed vantage point. Speed: extreme temporal compression where hours of environmental motion play out across a few seconds. Framing: hold the architectural or landscape composition rock-solid while shadows sweep, clouds stream, and lights or crowds streak through the scene. End: finish on the same locked framing after visible passage of time.

moves.name: Pass-through objects
moves.intent: Impossible cinema-magic camera flight that threads straight through a narrow window, mirror, gap, or barrier into a new room beyond.
moves.when_to_use: Seamless scene transitions, crossing from exterior to interior through glass or an opening, or revealing a hidden chamber.
moves.prompt: Camera: precision forward pass-through glide. Movement: fly straight forward toward a window, aperture, or foreground barrier and pass seamlessly through the opening into the space behind it. Speed: smooth, uninterrupted forward momentum. Framing: center the opening or surface as the camera approaches so its edges sweep past the periphery during the threshold crossing. End: emerge cleanly inside the newly revealed interior or environment beyond.
